title: Endogenous Biotinylated Proteins Cause Artefacts in Western Blot Studies
author: Grant, Shapiro, et al.
materials: Monoclonal antibodies 6E10 (200 μg) or a combination of 13.1.1 and 2.1.3 (anti-Aβ40 and anti-Aβ42, respectively, 100 μg each, gift of Dr. Pritam Das, Mayo Clinic, Jacksonville, FL) were covalently linked to Protein-G coupled magnetic beads (500 μL bead slurry, Protein G Mag Sepharose, Cat # 28951379, GE Healthcare Life Sciences), according to the following protocol. Beads were washed three times with IPDB containing protease and phosphatase inhibitors (1 mL buffer/500 μL bead-slurry equivalent), then re-suspended in 1 mL IPDB with protease inhibitors added (0.1 mM PMSF, 0.2 mM 1,10-PTH, and 1× protease inhibitor cocktail, Sigma-Aldrich). Antibodies were then added, and the mixture was incubated overnight at 4 °C, with mixing. Buffer with unbound antibody was then removed, and beads were washed one time with 1 mL IPDB, and one time with 1 mL triethanolamine (TEA, 200 mM, pH 9.0). Beads were then incubated for 15 min, room temperature, with mixing, in 1 mL 200 mM TEA with 50 mM dimethyl pimelimidate dihydrochloride, in order to crosslink the antibodies to the beads. Following crosslinking, beads were washed once with 1 mL 200 mM TEA, pH 9.0, and then the reaction was quenched by incubating the beads in 1 mL 10% (v/v) ethanolamine, for 15 min at room temperature, with mixing. The quenching solution was then removed, and the beads were washed once with 100 mM glycine-HCl, pH 2.8 with 2 M urea, and then three times with IPDB (1 mL solution per wash). Beads were stored in 12 mL IP buffer B with the protease inhibitors listed above, at 4 °C.

Frozen mouse brain lysates were thawed on ice, and then centrifuged at 9600×g for 10 min, 4 °C to remove any cryoprecipitates. Lysate (containing 1.5–2 mg protein) was added to the anti-Aβ40/42 immunoaffinity matrix (with fresh protease inhibitors added), and incubated overnight at 4 °C, with mixing. The buffer was then removed, and the beads were washed with 12 mL IP buffer B with 1% (v/v) Triton X-100. Captured proteins were then eluted using 333 μL elution buffer (33 mM glycine-HCl, 1% (w/v) Octyl β-D-1-thioglucopyranoside (Cat # O6004, Sigma-Aldrich), pH 2.8). The elution step was repeated two more times.

steps.title: Wash and Resuspend Protein G Beads
steps.instruction: Place 500 µL Protein‑G magnetic bead slurry (Cat # 28951379, GE Healthcare) in a tube; wash three times with 1 mL IPDB containing protease and phosphatase inhibitors (1 mL per 500 µL bead equivalent). After the final wash, resuspend the beads in 1 mL IPDB supplemented with 0.1 mM PMSF, 0.2 mM 1,10‑PTH, and 1× Sigma‑Aldrich protease inhibitor cocktail.

steps.title: Couple Antibodies to Beads
steps.instruction: Add either 200 µg monoclonal 6E10 antibody or 100 µg each of antibodies 13.1.1 and 2.1.3 (anti‑Aβ40 and anti‑Aβ42) to the resuspended beads, then incubate overnight at 4 °C with gentle mixing. After incubation, discard the supernatant containing unbound antibody.

steps.title: Crosslink Antibodies and Quench
steps.instruction: Wash beads once with 1 mL IPDB, then once with 1 mL 200 mM triethanolamine (TEA), pH 9.0. Incubate beads for 15 min at room temperature with mixing in 1 mL 200 mM TEA containing 50 mM dimethyl pimelimidate dihydrochloride to crosslink the antibodies. Wash once with 1 mL 200 mM TEA (pH 9.0). Quench the reaction by incubating beads for 15 min at room temperature with mixing in 1 mL 10 % (v/v) ethanolamine. Remove the quench solution, wash once with 1 mL 100 mM glycine‑HCl, pH 2.8 containing 2 M urea, then wash three times with 1 mL IPDB each. Store the prepared beads in 12 mL IP buffer B containing the same protease inhibitors at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Mouse Brain Lysate
steps.instruction: Thaw frozen mouse brain lysates on ice, then centrifuge at 9 600 × g for 10 min at 4 °C to remove cryoprecipitates. Keep the supernatant (containing 1.5–2 mg total protein) on ice and add fresh protease inhibitors before use.

steps.title: Immunoaffinity Capture and Elution
steps.instruction: Add the lysate (1.5–2 mg protein) to the anti‑Aβ40/42 immunoaffinity matrix (prepared beads) with fresh protease inhibitors and incubate overnight at 4 °C with mixing. Remove the incubation buffer, wash the beads with 12 mL IP buffer B containing 1 % (v/v) Triton X‑100. Elute bound proteins three times by adding 333 µL elution buffer (33 mM glycine‑HCl, 1 % (w/v) Octyl β‑D‑1‑thioglucopyranoside, Cat # O6004, Sigma‑Aldrich, pH 2.8), incubating briefly, and collecting the eluate each time.

steps.title: Sequential Immunopurification (Optional)
steps.instruction: First, apply 1.5–2 mg lysate to a 6E10 immunoaffinity matrix with fresh protease inhibitors and perform incubation, wash, and three elutions exactly as described for the anti‑Aβ40/42 matrix. Pool the three 6E10 eluates, add protease inhibitors, and concentrate the pool ~2‑fold using a Vacu‑fuge. Remove 35 µL for Western blot analysis; apply the remaining eluate to the anti‑Aβ40/42 matrix and repeat the overnight incubation, 12 mL Triton X‑100 wash, and three elutions as above.
